terms.grammar: sī with nōn before the word negated; alone after a first condition
evidence: Phaedr. 4 epil. 7: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā
Varr. RR 1.11.2: sī nōn, quam proximē
terms.comment: Negates one word, not the whole condition (for that, nisi: see unless); also “if not”, “failing that”, after a first condition.

terms.grammar: conjunction: the second of two conditions, the other way
evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.4.3: sī est spēs nostrī reditūs … sīn, ut ego metuō, trānsāctum est
Cic. Att. 1.2.1: sīn aliter acciderit, hūmāniter ferēmus
terms.comment: After sī: “but if”. With the verb left out, sīn minus or sīn aliter, “but if not”.

terms.grammar: sī with minus, the verb understood
evidence: Cic. Rep. 3.7: sī minus sapientēs, at certē summā laude dignōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “If not this, at least that”: Lewis & Short gives it as the same as sīn minus.

phrases.latin: sī nōn ingenium, certē brevitātem approbā
phrases.english: if not my talent, at least approve my brevity

phrases.latin: vīlla aedificanda potissimum ut intrā saepta vīllae habeat aquam, sī nōn, quam proximē
phrases.english: the farmhouse should above all be built with water inside its walls, or if not, as near as possible

phrases.latin: quem sī legēs, laetābor; sīn autem minus, habēbunt certē quō sē oblectent posterī
phrases.english: if you read it, I shall be glad; but if not, those who come after will at least have something to enjoy

phrases.latin: sī est spēs nostrī reditūs, eam cōnfīrmēs et rem adjuvēs; sīn, ut ego metuō, trānsāctum est, quōquō modō potes ad mē fac veniās.
phrases.english: if there is hope of my return, strengthen it and help the cause; but if, as I fear, it is all over, come to me any way you can.
